phase_note: DEVELOPMENT result; not reportable. Documents a fixture-authoring bug fix, not a measurement.

issue.description: cases/case_d_ccs2/judgment/judgment_record.json's signature.signing_time was 2026-03-02T15:08:00Z, but that same document's disposition_decisions[D-02] and selections[JD-CCS2-SEL-002] were dated 2026-03-09T15:05:00Z -- a signature seven days before the latest decision it attests to. A judgment record cannot be validly signed before the decisions it records were made.
issue.detected_by: Independent manuscript-vs-repo reconciliation research this session, cross-referenced against cases/case_d_ccs2/judgment/judgment_record.json directly.

root_cause.description: Signing timestamps (acs/dispositions/judgment) were hardcoded constants (2026-03-02T15:10/15:12/15:08Z) shared across all three CCS variants. tools/case_d_control.py's build_judgment_ccs2() was correctly authored with a later D-02 decision_time/selection_time (2026-03-09T15:05:00Z), reflecting the CCS2 narrative ("governance LATER issues policy 4.3"), but _write_variant's shared signing-time constants were never parametrized to let CCS2's signatures postdate its own later content -- an oversight when CCS2 was added as a third variant of a two-variant template.

resolution.approach: Fixed at the generator source, not by hand-editing the committed JSON. _write_variant now accepts acs_signing_time/dispositions_signing_time/judgment_signing_time overrides (defaulting to the original CCS0/CCS1 constants, so those two variants are byte-for-byte unaffected). CCS2's call site now passes 2026-03-09T15:10:00Z / 15:12:00Z / 15:08:00Z -- the exact same minute-offsets-after-the-latest-decision pattern already used for CCS0/CCS1 (decide, then sign ~3-8 minutes later), shifted to CCS2's real, later decision date instead of predating it.
resolution.why_not_move_the_decision_instead: The alternative (moving the D-02 decision/selection to on-or-before 2026-03-02) would contradict the manuscript's own narrative for CCS2 (policy 4.3 and the widening are explicitly LATER than the original CCS0/CCS1 governance), and would make CCS2 indistinguishable in chronology from CCS1's original emergency-exception grant. Moving the signature forward instead of the decision backward preserves the case's intended meaning.
resolution.regenerated_via: python -m tools.build_case_d (the existing, already-relied-upon Case D generator -- not a one-off script).

verification.note_on_signature_b64_unchanged: sign_document's Ed25519 signature covers the document's substantive content, not the signing_time metadata attached alongside it -- consistent with this project's own stated convention that the signature envelope is provenance metadata, not part of what is cryptographically bound to canonical content.
verification.case_d_matrix_after_fix: 10/10 (D9 widening-invalidation and D10 key/order-equivalence both still pass)
